## Why This Is Asked

This tests advanced observability design across multi-cloud Kubernetes, including OpenTelemetry, centralized logging, and runtime policy governance, plus CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry exporter configuration per service
- Central OTLP collector integration
- Loki trace-id linkage in logs

## Code Example

```yaml
# minimal deployment fragment enabling OTLP and traceable logs
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-example
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: myrepo/svc-example:latest
          env:
            - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
              value: "http://otlp-collector-collector:4317"
            - name: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES

## Why This Is Asked

Checks for API deprecation are common, and beginner-friendly gates show practical CI thinking without complex tooling.

## Key Concepts

- K8s API version deprecations
- CI gates in GitHub Actions
- Simple shell scripting for manifest checks
- Local verification versus PR gating

## Code Example

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
for f in k8s/**/*.yaml; do
  if grep -E \"apiVersion:\s*(extensions/v1beta1|apps/v1beta1|networking.k8s.io/v1beta1)\" \"$f\" >/dev/null; then
    echo \"Deprecated apiVersion found in $f\"
    exit 1
  fi
done
```

- How would you automatically fix or suggest updates and handle non-YAML files?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests practical, auditable governance for multi-team clusters beyond image/security gates.

Key Concepts

- Namespace governance with ResourceQuota and LimitRange
- Namespace-scoped RBAC and ServiceAccounts
- Lightweight CI gates using kubectl/yq
- Local validation vs CI parity

Code Example

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  kubectl -n "$ns" get resourcequota >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing ResourceQuota in $ns"; exit 1; }
  kubectl -n "$ns" get limitrange >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing LimitRange in $ns"; exit 1; }
  for dep in $(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {/end}'); do
    sa=$(kubectl -n "$ns" get deploy "$dep" -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}')
    if [ -z "$sa" ]; then echo "Deployment $dep in $ns uses default SA"; exit 1; fi
    kubectl -n "$ns" get rolebinding | grep -q "$sa" || { echo "Missing RBAC for $sa in $ns"; exit 1; }
  done
done
```

Failing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: team-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: rq
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    requests.memory: 8Gi
    limits.memory: 16Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: lr
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "4"
      memory: 8Gi
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sa-team-a-view
  namespace: team-a
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sa-team-a
  namespace: team-a
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: view
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      name: app
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: sa-team-a
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.21
```

Verification

- Locally: run the gate script against your cluster context and verify it fails/passes as expected; inspect output for missing quota/limitrange or RBAC gaps.
- CI: run the same script in a workflow step; ensure failing manifests fail the build and passing manifests pass.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of namespace isolation and basic egress filtering using NetworkPolicy. It checks hands-on ability to craft minimal, enforceable rules and verify them.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicy basics
- Namespace-scoped isolation
- Egress rules and default deny
- Basic verification via kubectl and logs

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-egress-isolate
  namespace: test
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.2.3/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
        except:
        - 255.255.255.255/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod in test namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 300"]
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod in test namespace (tries to access prod)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-pod
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "wget http://prod.svc.cluster.local || true"]
```

```yaml
# DNS test Pod (for compliance with DNS allow rule)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-test
  namespace: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local"]
```

## Follow-up Steps
- kubectl apply -f policy.yaml
- kubectl apply -f compliant-pod.yaml; kubectl exec compliant-pod -- curl logs.internal:443
- kubectl apply -f noncompliant-pod.yaml; observe failure to reach prod
- Check events: kubectl describe networkpolicy/test-egress-isolate -n test

## Why This Is Asked
Why this angle matters: binds image attestation, SBOM, secret management, and canary verification across clouds, aligning with production-grade trust.

## Key Concepts
- Sigstore cosign attestation
- SBOM requirements
- SecretStore-based injection
- Kyverno/OPA admission gates
- Canary release with Prometheus SLOs

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy example
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sigstore-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: audit
  rules:
  - name: attest-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment, StatefulSet]
    validate:
      message: "image must be cosigned and SBOM present"
      pattern:
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]: "*"
        metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"]: "*"
```

```rego
# OPA policy (high level)
package gatekeeper
violation[{"msg": msg}]
default violation = []
violation = [{"msg": m} |
  input.request.kind == "Deployment" and
  not input.request.object.spec.template.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/signature"]
  or not input.request.object.metadata.annotations["cosign.sigstore.dev/sbom"] ]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this in CI for new service manifests?
- How would you handle SBOM provenance across registries?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests basic understanding of Kubernetes security posture and practical gate design in CI, covering both Pod security and NetworkPolicy defaults.

## Key Concepts
- Pod securityContext and container.securityContext
- Kyverno vs OPA Gatekeeper for policy enforcement
- Default-deny NetworkPolicy per Namespace
- Local validation with kubectl and kyverno/opa tooling
- CI validation with GitHub Actions hooks

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy (minimal)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secctx
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: check-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and runAsNonRoot: true"
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              runAsNonRoot: true
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# NetworkPolicy default-deny (Namespace scope)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt the policy to exclude specific namespaces or namespaces with legacy workloads?
- How would you test this in a multi-tenant CI environment with limited cluster access?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement real-world security gates that combine image scanning, attestation, and policy enforcement in a scalable multi‑tenant environment.

## Key Concepts

- Admission control with OPA/Kyverno
- SBOMs and CVE scoring via Trivy
- Image signing with cosign and Rekor attestation
- PR‑level gating and local verification

## Code Example

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: scan SBOM, sign, and publish attestation
name: Security Gate
on: [pull_request]
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  - name: Run Trivy SBOM
    run: trivy image --format cyclonedx -o sbom.json image:tag
  - name: Cosign sign SBOM
    run: cosign sign -key cosign.pub sbom.json
  - name: Rekor attestation
    run: cosign attest sbom.json --type sbom --format json
```

```yaml
# OPA policy (partial) enforcing CVE threshold and SBOM signing
package gate
default allow = false
allow {
  input.images[_].cve_score <= 6.0
  input.images[_].sbom_signed
}
```

```yaml
# Minimal manifest examples (one failing, one passing)

  name: example-fail

        image: registry.example/unsafe:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# passing: compliant image
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example/secure:1.0.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

- How would you scale the gate across many clusters and tenants?

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates expertise in multi-cloud tenancy, data residency compliance, and automated policy enforcement. - **Network policy enforcement**: Per-tenant egress gateways with namespace-aware NetworkPolicies ensure traffic cannot leak across tenant boundaries.

- **Service mesh integration**: SPIRE provides automated certificate management, but admission policies must ensure workloads are properly registered before receiving traffic.

- **Progressive delivery with SLO gates**: Integrating Prometheus metrics into the deployment pipeline enables data-driven rollout decisions that protect production reliability.

## Why This Is Asked
This tests policy design across admission controls and CI gates for GPU workloads in a multi-tenant cluster.

## Key Concepts
- Kyverno policy design; - GPU resource constraints; - NodeSelector and labels; - Image signing with cosign; - CI validation and test manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno validation policy enforcing nodeSelector and tenant label for GPU deployments
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: gpu-tenant-isolation
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-node-selector-for-gpu
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: "Deployments requesting GPUs must have nodeSelector and tenant label"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              nodeSelector:
                nvidia.com/gpu: present
  - name: require-tenant-label
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: "Deployment must carry tenant label"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          labels:
            tenant: "*"
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions snippet to verify cosign and Kyverno
name: gpu-gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: cosign verify
        run: cosign verify <image>@<digest>
      - name: kyverno test
        run: kubectl apply -f test-manifests/ && kyverno test ./policies
```
